_provenance.experiment: Re-run of the Stan ADVI arm of the three SVI PPLBench models under a single uniform CmdStan ADVI budget setting that lets Stan's own convergence heuristic actually fire on logistic_regression. Supersedes the Stan ADVI entries of sec53_matched_init_suite_2026-07-14.json (stan_advi_matched_init) as the source for the Stan (VI) bars of paper/figures/baselines_bar_v2_data.json.
_provenance.motivation: Under the previous setting the Stan ADVI arm failed CmdStan's own convergence check on ALL FOUR logistic-regression trials, so the bar was drawn hollow/hatched in fig:baselines-bar.

diagnostic_mechanism.emitter: CmdStan stan/src/stan/variational/advi.hpp:430-439 prints 'Informational Message: The maximum number of iterations is reached! The algorithm may not have converged.' when the stochastic-gradient-ascent loop exits because iter_counter == max_iterations instead of because the rolling relative-ELBO test fired.
diagnostic_mechanism.test: advi.hpp:400-408. Every eval_elbo (default 100) iterations CmdStan estimates the ELBO from elbo_samples (default 100) draws, pushes rel_difference(elbo, elbo_prev) = |elbo_prev - elbo| / |elbo| into a circular buffer of size cb_size = max(0.1 * iter / eval_elbo, 2), and stops when the buffer MEAN or MEDIAN drops below tol_rel_obj (default 0.01).
diagnostic_mechanism.consumer: cmdstanpy 1.3.0 model.py:1565-1582 regex-matches the literal 'The algorithm may not have converged.' in the CmdStan console transcript; with require_converged=True it raises RuntimeError, with require_converged=False (what the harness uses) it downgrades to a logged WARNING and returns the fit. Nothing machine-readable was recorded before 2026-07-29.
diagnostic_mechanism.harness_recording_added_2026-07-29: stan_harness.py _advi_transcript_diagnostics() now parses the same transcript and records converged / stop_reason / final_iter / final_elbo / delta_elbo_mean / delta_elbo_med / the last ten ELBO rows into outputs/<run>/svi_diagnostics/stan_<model>_seed<seed>.json, and prints one 'Stan ADVI [seed N]: converged=...' line per trial.

_provenance.root_cause: NOT an iteration-budget problem and NOT a bad optimum. CmdStan's eta (step-size) adaptation is a greedy scan over eta in {100, 10, 1, 0.1, 0.01} that runs adapt_iter (default 50) SGD steps per candidate and stops at the first candidate whose post-scan ELBO is worse than the previous candidate's (advi.hpp:163-291). With the harness's protocol-matching grad_samples=1 the per-candidate ELBO estimate is so noisy that the scan stops one step early on roughly half the trial seeds and returns eta=10. At eta=10 the iterate random-walks with an amplitude that keeps the rolling relative-ELBO difference near 0.1-0.2 forever: raising iter to 100000 does not help (see ladder rung C2, delta_elbo_mean still 0.082 after 100000 iterations / 123 s). logistic_regression is the only one of the three models exposed to this because its |ELBO| is about 50, so the same absolute ELBO jitter is 60x larger relative to |ELBO| than on robust (|ELBO| ~ 7700) or n_schools (|ELBO| ~ 7070), whose median test clears 0.01 within a few hundred iterations.

chosen_setting.statement: Stan's ADVI runs its own algorithm with THREE budgets raised: grad_samples = 10 (CmdStan 2.38 default 1), adapt_iter = 200 (CmdStan default 50), iter = 30000 (CmdStan default 10000). algorithm = meanfield, elbo_samples = 100, eta adaptation engaged, tol_rel_obj = 0.01, eval_elbo = 100 are all left at CmdStan's defaults. draws = 200 = the protocol's K. Same matched CmdStan `inits` as before.
chosen_setting.cmdstan_2_38_defaults_verified: Read from CmdStan 2.38.0 stan/src/stan/services/experimental/advi/defaults.hpp (gradient_samples::default_value() = 1, adapt_iterations::default_value() = 50, elbo_samples = 100, max_iterations = 10000, tol_rel_obj = 0.01, eval_elbo = 100) and cross-checked against the CmdStan console banner, which prints 'grad_samples = 1 (Default)'. NOTE: cmdstanpy 1.3.0's own docstring (model.py:1473-1474) claims 'grad_samples ... Default is 10', which is WRONG for CmdStan 2.38; do not cite it. The harness's previous grad_samples = 1 therefore coincided with CmdStan's default, so raising it to 10 is a genuine third deviation, not the removal of an imposed one.
chosen_setting.why_grad_samples_10_is_load_bearing: grad_samples = 10 is what makes CmdStan's greedy eta scan reliable. At grad_samples = 1 no adapt_iter value works: adapt_iter = 50 returns eta = 10 on some seeds (ladder L0/C1), and adapt_iter = 100/200/500 returns eta = 100 on seed 2993578, which diverges to ELBO -4.5e5 .. -4.1e7 and held-out PLL -4.0e5 .. -4.1e7 while still reporting 'converged' because a static astronomically-bad ELBO trivially satisfies the relative test (ladder C4/C6/C9/C10). A hollow bar is preferable to that. Raising grad_samples when ADVI misbehaves is also what the cmdstanpy interface itself suggests (model.py:1593-1596 emits 'Double the value of argument "grad_samples"' on a gradient failure), though that message targets a gradient exception rather than non-convergence.
chosen_setting.why_eta_cannot_simply_be_pinned: adapt_engaged = 0 (pin eta to CmdStan's default value 1) is not usable with cmdstanpy 1.3.0: CmdStanVB.__init__ -> stancsv.parse_variational_eta requires the 'Stepsize adaptation complete. / eta = X' comment block that CmdStan only writes when adaptation is engaged, so the fit dies with 'ValueError: Unable to parse eta from Stan CSV, adaptation block not found' (ladder C8).
chosen_setting.uniformity: The identical three-knob setting is applied to the Stan ADVI arm of ALL THREE SVI models. It is recorded in pplbench_configs/svi/{logistic_regression,robust_regression,n_schools}_matched_init.json (the Stan-only protocol configs that produced the figure numbers) and in the stan block of pplbench_configs/svi/{logistic_regression,robust_regression,n_schools}.json.
chosen_setting.not_changed: model, data, generator seed, metric, K = 200 draws, 4 trials, matched init point, thread count, and every other arm.

_provenance.env: CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''), 32 threads, 192 cores, cmdstanpy 1.3.0, CmdStan 2.38.0, probprog-bench python. Sole benchmark job on the machine.
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains SVI, unchanged: iterations = 200 (K = 200 draws from the fitted mean-field guide), num_warmup = 0, 4 trials, model seed 12345, shared trial seeds [1396133, 2993578, 6164479, 9523583]. Only the guide fit is timed; compile is separate. overall n_eff = arviz ESS over all latent sites with the 4 trials as 4 chains; n_eff/s median = n_eff median / steady-state (trials 1..3) fit wall time. PLL = per-trial final cumulative (logsumexp-over-draws) predictive log-likelihood on the held-out items.

quality_check_against_nuts.logistic_regression_nuts_reference: All four NUTS arms of sec53_matched_init_suite_2026-07-14.json agree on this model: held-out PLL -30.23 to -30.72, posterior alpha = -12.55 +/- 2.06, beta = [2.766, 0.725, -0.577, 0.755, -2.583, -2.975, -0.299, 1.009, -4.312, 5.153] (recomputed from outputs/2026-07-14_16:56:57 / 16:59:03 / 16:59:39 samples.nc, post-warmup).
quality_check_against_nuts.verdict: Judged against that NUTS posterior the CONVERGED Stan ADVI fit is the BEST of the three mean-field VI fits on logistic regression, not a worse one. Pooled posterior means: Stan ADVI new alpha -9.887 (sd 0.539), beta [2.175, 0.555, -0.448, 0.556, -2.066, -2.342, -0.358, 0.786, -3.389, 4.058]; Stan ADVI old (non-converged) alpha -24.388 (sd 8.706), beta up to 10.136, i.e. overshooting by ~2x with an 8.7-wide alpha; NumPyro/Impulse/Turing ADVI alpha -1.62 (sd 0.155), beta [0.354, 0.503, -0.086, 0.209, -0.41, -0.384, -0.556, 0.111, -0.55, 0.66], i.e. still essentially at the loc = 0 initialization.
quality_check_against_nuts.consequence_for_the_paper_band: The -71.6 / -72.1 / -76.0 logistic VI 'band' is where a FIXED 2000-step Adam(0.01) budget lands, not where the model's posterior is. The converged Stan ADVI PLL of -27.30 is above that band and next to the NUTS value of -30.3 (PLL is a logsumexp over the K draws, so a guide whose scales match the posterior scores higher than a near-degenerate one). Any prose that treats -72 as the reference band for this model needs this caveat.

_provenance.n_eff_caveat: For a VI arm the PPLBench trials-as-chains ESS measures across-restart reproducibility RELATIVE TO the fitted guide's own scale, so a tight-but-reproducible under-converged guide scores far higher than a converged guide with SGD restart noise. On logistic the converged Stan guide has across-trial location spread ~0.09-0.20 on beta while its own fitted sd on the well-identified coordinates beta[8], beta[9] is only 0.0075 / 0.0089, a ratio of ~18, so split-Rhat is large and the pooled ESS stays around 19 even though the four fits agree on the ELBO to ~1% and on the site means to ~2-4%. Converging harder cannot close this: the SGD stopping-point noise falls only as 1/sqrt(iterations), so an 18x reduction would need ~300x the budget.

figure_data_delta.why_all_three_drop: grad_samples = 10 is 10x the per-iteration work of CmdStan's default grad_samples = 1, and the eta scan now costs 5 x 200 instead of 5 x 50 iterations. On logistic that buys convergence (n_eff median 5.48 -> 18.81) but the fit wall time rises 2.26 s -> 15.06 s. robust and n_schools already converged, so for them the uniform setting is pure added cost (3.88 s and 3.93 s per fit against 0.65 s and 0.46 s).
